explanation: The article gives the mechanism in one sentence: "Members of the Balkan League, seeing how easily Italy defeated the Ottomans and motivated by incipient Balkan nationalism, attacked the Ottoman Empire in October 1912, starting the First Balkan War a few days before the end of the Italo-Turkish War." The sentence names two things that moved the League, and only one of them is this war. What Italy supplied was the demonstration that the Ottoman army could be beaten. The nationalism that wanted to beat it came from elsewhere. A demonstration of weakness is a condition the later war was fought on rather than the act that began it, so the edge takes the weaker of the two types the source allows. The same lead calls the war "a precursor of World War I", which dates the war against another one and names no mechanism, so no edge is written from it. The confidence is probable, because Wikipedia is the only source and rule 22 will not let that stand as consensus.
